title: Tamarind-Mandarin Wok Glaze
description: Tamarind and mandarin juice give this mild wok glaze a bright sweet-tart flavor balanced by coconut aminos.

steps.title: Dissolve the tamarind
steps.text: Whisk {tamarind} into {mandarin} in the cool HexClad wok until smooth.

steps.title: Reduce the glaze base
steps.text: Add {broth}, {aminos}, {sugar} and {garlic}. Simmer uncovered for 5–8 minutes, stirring, until the liquid measures just under 1 cup.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the glaze in a heatproof cup and add a little hot water, if needed, to reach 1 cup.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Turn fully cooked poached chicken or fish gently in the glaze off heat. Spoon the remaining glaze over the plated portions.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Mix the mandarin and tamarind up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Thicken the sauce just before serving. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in small portions for up to 2 months. Stir while reheating to recover the sheen. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses both tamarind and mandarin. For gentler Option B, omit the tamarind and use unsweetened pear juice in place of mandarin. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 17 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 4.0 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 27 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
